text:
Anya: seeing a weird p95 east-west climb ~35-50ms specifically during the 08:10-08:20 batching window in us-west-2. not constant, looks like stair-stepped jumps. any quick checks?
infra-bot: [alert] increased p95 latency on cluster gw-usw2-gpu between 2026-03-12T08:10:00Z - 2026-03-12T08:20:00Z. affected nodes: gpu-rack7-[12..18].
Sam: can you paste node list and raw p95 series? also which batch size/profile was running?
Anya: batch profile = gen-large (seq=1024, batch=24). nodes: gpu-rack7-12,13,14,15,16,17,18. here's the p95 trace snippet: ```08:08 12ms, 08:10 48ms, 08:12 44ms, 08:14 13ms, 08:16 46ms, 08:18 49ms```
Miguel: thanks. first guess: intermittent MTU negotiation/PMTUD issues or RDMA fallback to TCP in path. can you check dmesg on one of the nodes?
Anya: grabbing dmesg from gpu-rack7-15; quick grep shows: ```mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: mlx5: reported MTU change from 9000 to 1500 on vf 3```
Zara: whoa, MTU flaps. did we recently roll any ToR configs or BGP changes? network change log shows none in that window.
Kai: also check if our SR-IOV/VF hotplug happened from k8s eviction during batch spikes. SR-IOV can reattach and cause mgmt to reset VF MTU.
Sam: run ethtool -S on peer interfaces and rdma stats. also check if any path retrains on the switches.
Miguel: pasted quick outputs from gpu-rack7-15 -> gpu-rack7-16 interconnect: ```# ethtool -S ens192 | head -n 20 rx_missed_errors: 0 rx_crc_errors: 0 tx_queue_0_drops: 0 rx_no_buff: 0 xmit_more_work: 0``` and RDMA counters: ```rxe_read_requests: 0 rxe_read_errors: 7 rxe_recv_queue_overflow: 3```
Anya: rxe_read_errors and recv overflow look suspicious. also kube logs show brief pod restarts on node 16 during 08:12.
Zara: could be a noisy neighbor or a hardware NIC hiccup. can we correlate with power/thermal events? I see a spike in GPU power draw at 08:11 on rack7-14 (from telemetry).
Kai: immediate mitigation: reduce gen-large batch from 24->16 on the affected lane for next hour and enable cross-rack spill to avoid pegging the same p2p paths. that should smooth the staircase pattern.
Sam: agree. also create a short-lived route policy to bias traffic to alternate fabric paths for those nodes while we debug. I'll prepare the k8s rollout and network policy.
Miguel: scheduling deeper net-debug: please run packet captures for a couple of windows, and enable mlx5 debug logs at info level. snippet to run on node: ```sudo tcpdump -i ens192 -w /tmp/ew-pktdump-$(date +%s).pcap 'tcp'```. and: ```sudo ethtool -K ens192 gro off gso off tso off```
Anya: starting tcpdump on 15 and 16 now. will keep captures for next two windows. applying temporary batch change in deployments - rolling patch 1/7.
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2431: "staggered EW latency during peak batching - rack7" and assigned to eng-infra + netops. link: https://tickets.internal/INFRA-2431
Zara: good. next steps: 1) collect pcaps + RDMA counters for 3 windows, 2) netops to check ToR logs for VF/MTU events, 3) if HW suspected, schedule NIC vendor debug on impacted hosts.
Sam: I'll push the route tweak and monitor p95. if mitigation holds, we can mark low-sev and continue root-cause.
Anya: thanks all. will drop captures and a short summary in the ticket once done. :thumbsup:
